licenses.text:
Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Willibald Alexis (author, Wikidata Q77312), died 1871; Walter Scott (other, Wikidata Q79025), died 1832; Thomas De Quincey (translator, Wikidata Q317160), died 1859. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Alexis, Willibald, 1798-1871; Scott, Walter, 1771-1832 [Dubious author]; De Quincey, Thomas, 1785-1859 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Walladmor, London : Printed for Taylor and Hessey, 1825, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/walladmor01dequ. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 68%, 91% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Willibald Alexis, Thomas De Quincey, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
